beats.say: A key file for your cloud account sits in a Secret.
beats.text: A key file in a Secret

beats.say: It is valid for years. And it works from any machine that has a copy.
beats.label: The risk
beats.head: Valid for years, from anywhere

beats.say: This port has two ideas: the identity of a pod, and cloud access with no keys.
beats.label: Port 9 · Workload identity

check.prompt: What does a pod use to prove who it is to the API server?
options: A short-lived token of its service account
check.why: The node mounts a token for the pod's service account. It expires and is rotated.

beats.say: First: every pod has an identity.
A pod runs as a service account. The node gives it a token for that account.
beats.label: Service account
beats.head: A token for each pod

beats.say: The token lives for about an hour, and stops when the pod is deleted.
beats.label: Short-lived
beats.head: About one hour, then renewed

beats.say: The token says who you are. Access control decides what you may do.
beats.label: Two questions
beats.head: Who you are, then what you may do

beats.say: Second: reach the cloud with no key file.
The cloud trusts the service account of the cluster. You grant a role to it.
beats.label: Workload identity
beats.head: The cloud trusts the pod identity

beats.say: The pod gets a short cloud token when it asks. Nothing to store, nothing to rotate.
beats.label: The result
beats.head: No key to leak or rotate

beats.say: One service account per app. Tokens are short-lived. And no key files.
beats.label: Workload identity

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
